rappel_detail.notes: Rope-stretching rappel down to an anchor of three fixed nuts.
rappel_detail.station: Top of the descent gully: slung block with a nut and piton

rappel_detail.notes: Lands on a large ledge; downclimb leftward to a small tree. Tricky under early-season snow, but other trees allow shorter intermediate raps.
Lands on a large terrace; scramble down and a bit left to a small tree hidden behind a big white block.
Goes down the waterfall slabs, moving hard to the right across the stream to a big slung block.
rappel_detail.station: Small tree behind the white block

rappel_detail.notes: Late season this is a full 60 m to talus, with an optional 10 m rap off a pinch point on the left. Early season, a 30 m rap reaches moderate snow, with a bollard used for the steepest frozen part.
Reached by following the obvious ledge climber's left from the top. Full 60 m rope rappel.
Full 60 m rappel that also crosses the gully.
A full 60 m rope length lands on a grassy slope. Walk down the slope to the next tree.
Last rappel, to the ground.

bc_mount_bryce_3_507m_rice_cooker.descent_text: Follow the obvious ledge that leads climber's left until you reach a tree with rappel tat. Rappel from the tree, then use fixed nuts for the next anchor, which takes you across the gully. A third rappel from fixed nuts reaches a grassy slope, from which you hike down to a tree with tat and make the last rappel to the ground. Carry two 60 m ropes.

rappel_detail.notes: Follow the flake crack to a small tree; the station sits a few feet to its right. With two 60 m ropes, descend under the headwall, over one short vertical bit, to a second station that hides beneath the headwall and is hard to see until you are on it.
rappel_detail.anchor: rap station several feet right of the tree
rappel_detail.station: small tree beside the White Flake crack

rappel_detail.notes: Descend vertically to the anchor that caps the neighbouring Jabberwalky route; it sits atop a small arch and is likewise easy to miss from a distance.
A short rap reaches the next station.
rappel_detail.station: anchor at the top of Jabberwalky

rappel_detail.notes: A 60 m rap down the neighbouring Aoxomoxoa line ends at the big sandy ledge. Recommended for children or anyone unsure of Tuolumne friction.
A full 60 m rappel lands about 30 feet above the pin and nut station; a purple sling around a boulder allows the short hop down to it.
rappel_detail.anchor: sling with a locking carabiner at the summit

rappel_detail.notes: A second 60 m rappel only just reaches the snowfield, and may not reach once the snow melts back. Glissade the slope to your stash if conditions allow.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed pin and nut station with a red sling

rappel_detail.notes: Afterward, hike back down to the brink of the large pitch.
Afterward, hike down to the lip of the ice step below.
Reaches the creek bed below the chockstone. Ramble down the creek and downclimb toward P3, or traverse to a cluster of leaning trees west of the creek above the last step.
Rap first the short cliff that skirts the step, continuing the full way down P3 in one go. Hike to the next cliff and look for tree anchors.
Then walk out the way you came.
Down and climber's left past the pitch 3 belay to a slung block.
Straight down to a fixed nut in the right wall of a small side gully.
One last rappel to the ground.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed nut on the right wall of the mini-gully

rappel_detail.notes: Single rope. Below it, either downclimb the little step or use willows or trees on the descender's left.
Use two ropes; one rope might reach but is untested.
Simul-rappel with two ropes. Then downclimb the low-angle creek ice or rappel from trees or boulders.
rappel_detail.anchor: main pillar, or a V-thread if the ice is trustworthy

rappel_detail.notes: Single rope. Downclimb pitch 2 (best) or rig something off boulders or rim trees to the north; bypass pitch 1.

co_grand_mesa_2_watson.descent_text: Reverse the route pillar by pillar. Rappel the pillars from trees, boulders, chockstones or the belay arch, or from V-threads in the ice if you trust it. The big pillars take two ropes. Where the creek ice lies back, downclimb it, and walk around the lowest boulder-blocked step.

rappel_detail.notes: Hike back down to the base of pitch 1 for this rappel.
rappel_detail.anchor: rock pinch under the huge chockstone

rappel_detail.notes: Run the ropes through the bolts directly; two 60 m half ropes.
rappel_detail.station: high ledge system just right of the summit area of the unnamed peak, marked by two pointed upright rocks

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel to the snowfield. Alternative: walk the fourth class ridge down to Arapaho Pass, or continue to Mount Neva.
rappel_detail.station: pitch 2 ledge with dark rectangular blocks

co_mount_neva_peace_is_for_the_valleys_w.descent_text: From the top, walk and scramble to the flat summit area then find the ledge on the right-hand side marked by two upright pointed rocks. Bolted rappel anchors there lead down to a ledge with dark rock and a second set of anchors, and another rappel reaches the snowfield; two ropes are needed. Alternatively, take the fourth-class ridge down to Arapaho Pass, or keep going up the ridge to Mount Neva and descend one of its faces.
